title: Descent for quasi-coherent modules
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme and $\mathcal F$ a quasi-coherent
$\mathcal O_X$-module. Then the presheaf on the
small etale site of $X$ that
sends $u:U\to X$ to $\Gamma(U,u^*\mathcal F)$, with the pullback
restrictions, is a sheaf.
(*Classical input: Stacks Project, Descent, Section 35.8, Tag
[03DR](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03DR).*)

proof.text: Let a covering family in the small etale site of X be given. By the definition of the small etale topology and the etale-to-fpqc comparison, this family is an fpqc covering of its target.

Apply the fpqc descent statement for quasi-coherent modules to the pullback module on the target and to the compatible family of sections. It gives a unique section on the target whose pullbacks are the given sections; uniqueness is the uniqueness part of effective descent.

The presheaf is the assignment in the statement because its restriction maps are the pullback restrictions of the functoriality node. Thus the existence and uniqueness just proved are precisely the sheaf equalizer condition on the small etale site.
